chunks.arabic_text: سُئِلَ أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: عَنِ الْيَوْمِ الْمَشْكُوكِ فِيهِ

translations.en: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was asked about the doubtful day.

chunks.arabic_text: فَقَالَ «لَأَنْ أَصُومَ يَوْمًا مِنْ شَعْبَانَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ أَنْ أُفْطِرَ يَوْمًا مِنْ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ»

translations.en: He said: “That I fast one day from Sha'ban is more beloved to me than that I break the fast for one day from the month of Ramadan.”

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal preference regarding the day of doubt, when it is uncertain whether the day belongs to Sha'ban or Ramadan. Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام states that observing fasting as Sha'ban is preferable to risking failure to fast a day of Ramadan, highlighting caution in matters of obligatory sawm.
en.seo_question: What did Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام say about fasting on the day of doubt?

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, the title of Imam 'Ali عليه السلام
key_terms.الْيَوْمِ الْمَشْكُوكِ: the doubtful day, when it is uncertain whether it is Sha'ban or Ramadan
key_terms.أُفْطِرَ: I break the fast; to refrain from fasting
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, in which fasting is obligatory
